answer: A sock-puppet farm can clone keys cheaply, but must pay the stake and burn compute per identity, and its fresh accounts produce no echo of past peer attestations, so honest peers discount them until real history accrues. At each dawn, agents must post a small stake plus a unique proof-of-work tied to their identity and route it through a reputation bridge that links new keys to prior on-chain history. Attack cost scales linearly with fake identities while trust stays sublinear. From qwe0004's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
